title: Anion-exchange-resin-loaded chitosan/poly(vinyl alcohol) adsorptive composite films for selective Cr( vi ) uptake from high-salinity synthetic tannery effluent
content: Hexavalent chromium [Cr(vi)] is a highly mobile and toxic oxyanion whose selective removal from saline industrial effluents remains challenging. Here, glutaraldehyde-crosslinked poly(vinyl alcohol)/chitosan (PVA–CS) films loaded with 0–20 wt% of a strong-base anion exchange resin (AER) were prepared by solution casting and evaluated as self-supported adsorbents for Cr(vi). SEM and FTIR confirmed resin incorporation, and the ion-exchange capacity of the composites peaked at 2.60 meq g−1 at 14 wt% AER. The optimum film (P-C/14%A) removed 95.5% of Cr(vi) at pH 2.0, 2.33 g L−1 adsorbent, 30 mg L−1 Cr(vi), 30 °C and 60 min. Equilibrium data were described by both the Langmuir (R2 = 0.978; Qmax = 15.4 mg g−1) and Freundlich (R2 = 0.944; 1/n = 0.45) models, and the kinetics followed a pseudo-first-order profile. Thermodynamic analysis (ΔH = −44.3 kJ mol−1, ΔS = −122 J mol−1 K−1, ΔG = −7.9 to −6.1 kJ mol−1 over 298–313 K) indicated a spontaneous, exothermic process. In a synthetic tannery matrix containing more than 20 000 mg L−1 each of Na+, K+ and Cl−, the film removed 84.5% of Cr(vi), matching the free resin, while losing three-to five-fold less mass under acid and thermal stress. Removal declined only from 95% to 90% over four adsorption–desorption cycles, demonstrating a durable and fully recoverable adsorbent format.
